subject: Retention drift & compressed audit bundles — extraction options and timelines
messages:

Subject: Request: clarification on retention drift and compressed bundles

Hi Jonas,

Quick request from our SOC2 evidence team — we're reconciling retention windows between your admin-activity ledger and the export snapshots we received last week. A couple of specific asks:

- Can you confirm the TTL/retention policy applied to admin_activity events for hosted tenants (default and any per-account overrides)?
- For exports: what compressed bundle formats do you support (gzip tar, zipped parquet, ndjson.gz)? Any checksum metadata included in the manifest?
- If there are known scenarios where events are not included in a snapshot (e.g., ephemeral operator sessions older than X hours, or policy-driven truncation), please enumerate and give example timestamps we can use to validate.

We'd like a short runbook or a sample bundle (with redacted PII) so our auditors can validate extraction reproducibly. Target timeline: within 3 business days if possible.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: audit@acmehealth.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: clarification on retention drift and compressed bundles

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear checklist. High level answers up front, followed by a short playbook and attached sample bundle.

1) Retention policy
- Default: admin_activity events retained 180 days for hosted customers.
- Per-account overrides: Dedicated/Private customers can request extended retention (365/730 days) via contract; this is applied at the tenant level and recorded in the retention manifest.
- Retention drift scenarios: short-term drift can occur when a rolling snapshot is taken across shards during active garbage-collection; in practice we surface a manifest with token-level high-water marks to show what window was captured.

2) Export formats supported
- ndjson.gz (line-delimited JSON, gzipped) — standard for auditors because it’s easy to stream and diff.
- parquet (snappy) inside a .tar.gz wrapper — smaller size, schema enforced.
- CSV slices for quick sampling (not recommended for full forensic exports).
- Every bundle includes a manifest.json (SHA256 checksums for each file) and a signed manifest.sig when requested.

3) Exclusion scenarios
- Ephemeral operator sessions older than 7 days can be sampled out if they are marked as ephemeral by the operator framework; we annotate these as ephemeral:true in the event.
- Events trimmed by retention lifecycle during long-running snapshot: we include a "snapshot_range" block in the manifest to indicate earliest_included_ts and latest_included_ts.

Attached is a redacted sample bundle (audit-log-sample-2026-07.ndjson) and a retention matrix spreadsheet. Also linking our internal playbook for extraction: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-retention-playbook

If you prefer a parquet snapshot with signed manifest, tell me preferred compression and we can stage in an S3 share. I'll loop Kim (technical lead for evidence exports) and Marissa (custodial handoff) to coordinate the delivery window.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: audit-log-sample-2026-07.ndjson (12MB), retention-matrix-2026-07.xlsx (8KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Adding technical details for the auditor's validation team — small, copy-paste friendly operations notes.

- Export CLI (admin):
  redwoodctl export \\n    --tenant acmehealth \\n    --scope admin_activity \\n    --from 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z \\n    --to 2026-07-15T23:59:59Z \\n    --format parquet \\n    --compress gzip \\n    --manifest checksums \\n    --out s3://evidence-stage/acmehealth/2026-07-15-admin-parquet.tar.gz

- Manifest structure (included in every bundle):
  - bundle_id: uuid
  - earliest_included_ts: ISO8601
  - latest_included_ts: ISO8601
  - file_entries: list of {name, size_bytes, sha256}
  - signature: optional base64(sig) when "signed_manifest": true

- Checksum verification example (Linux):
  sha256sum audit-log-part-0001.parquet | awk '{print $1}'
  Compare to manifest file_entries[*].sha256

- Note on TTL/GC: our garbage collector runs in a weekend window for long-tail shards; if a snapshot intersects that window, earliest_included_ts may be slightly later than expected. We provide snapshot_range and also an adjacent capture (prior and next 4-hour slices) on request to show continuity.

If the auditors need an attested, time-stamped manifest with HSM-signed key, we can produce that under a short SOW.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Security — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
